title: Stateful checkpointed switchover controller + locked-plan IaC modules for zero-downtime private runtime upgrades
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a coordinated upgrade controller and accompanying locked-plan IaC modules to allow zero-downtime, tenant-isolated runtime/data-plane rollouts in VPC/private deployments. The controller will perform checkpointed state snapshots, produce immutable upgrade plans via Terraform modules, and execute staged cutovers using health-quorum checks and prewarm windows. Goal: allow safe, fast upgrades with deterministic rollback and minimal operator intervention for on-prem and VPC customers.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade controller can apply an immutable plan produced by Terraform modules and record the plan ID in the tenant ledger
Controller runs a checkpoint snapshot and validates KV/priming state before draining any traffic for a tenant slice
Health-quorum checks (probe pass rate, p50/p99 latency, error rate) evaluate per-tenant and block rollforward if thresholds breach
Rollback can be triggered automatically by controller within the canary window or manually via console/CLI and restores from latest checkpoint without data loss
Production pilot on 3 customers with varying workload profiles completes with <1% error-rate regression and <2x increase in 99th latency during cutover
Terraform IaC modules include a plan-locking artifact (signed plan blob) that the controller verifies before executing an upgrade
End-to-end e2e tests and chaos experiments validate rollback and state reconciliation flows
implementation_notes: Introduce terraform module redwood/upgrade_plan that outputs a signed plan blob and a plan-version tag stored in S3/attestation service
Controller extension: stateful-checkpoint step that triggers KV snapshot, stores metadata in tenant namespace, and creates a prewarm token for new runtime replicas
Health quorum: combine passive metrics (latency, errors) and active probes (synthetic prompts) weighted per-tenant SLA tier
Traffic shaping: implement gradual weight shift with pausepoints at 10%, 50%, 100% and configurable soak durations; default soak = 90s for canary
Rollback path: three-tier strategy: immediate abort during prewarm, staged revert to prior model variant+image using checkpointed state, and full evacuation+rollback for catastrophic failures
Require plan-lock verification on private control plane: controller will reject any plan whose signature does not match the stored plan artifact
Add feature flag to enable plan-lock verification per-cluster to allow gradual rollout to existing private customers
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Plan-locking vs fast iteration: we adopt signed plan blobs to prevent drift during upgrades at the cost of extra IaC pipeline step and storage of artifacts
Snapshot frequency: coarse (per-upgrade) snapshots chosen over continuous delta replication to reduce IO impact; tradeoff: longer rollback window and potential re-prime time
Health-quorum strictness: conservative default thresholds to protect customers but allow per-tenant tuning to avoid false positives on noisy workloads
Prewarm strategy: allocate minimal warm capacity to avoid cascading cost, which may lead to slightly longer first-token latencies post-cutover for cold tenants
progress_updates: 2025-03-02: Ticket created. Initial design proposal shared in Confluence (link below). Assigned to Ben Lawson.
2025-03-04: Terraform module skeleton implemented (redwood/upgrade_plan). Local plan signing prototype works. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1357
2025-03-06: Controller checkpoint API defined; proto reviewed by infra and runtime teams. Inline feedback to make snapshot async and idempotent.
2025-03-08: Health-quorum design reviewed with SRE; agreed on combining synthetic probes with passive metrics. Added per-tenant weight to avoid noisy tenant executions affecting global decisions.

2025-03-09: Integration test harness for tenant slice upgrades completed; initial runs show stable behavior for synthetic workload. Observed 1.6x tail latency spike at 100% weight -> tuning soak window.
2025-03-10: PRs updated per review; security requested plan-signature attestation. Added security review flag and scheduled meeting with Security on 2025-03-12.
test_plan: Unit tests for plan-signing and plan-lock verification (infra team)
Simulated tenant-slice upgrades in staging with 3 workload profiles: steady-state, bursty, and long-context
Chaos injection: node termination during prewarm and mid-cutover; verify controller retries and rollback
Canary pilot: run on 3 private deployments with low-impact tenants for 4 weeks before broad enablement
Metrics to monitor: per-tenant p50/p99 latency, error-rate, prewarm success rate, KV-snapshot duration, rollback success rate
rollback_playbook: Phase 0 (prewarm failure): abort upgrade and leave existing replicas serving. Emit alert and annotation with failed probe metrics.
Phase 1 (canary degrade): automatic rollback to previous plan-version using checkpointed state; controller performs staged revert and rebalances traffic.
Phase 2 (failed revert): escalate to manual runbook: collect snapshot artifacts, run diagnostic collector, coordinate with runtime SRE for live evacuation.
Phase 3 (post-incident): generate incident report, attach plan blob and probe timeline, add postmortem actions to this ticket and affected tenant issues
open_questions: How long do we retain signed plan blobs and tenant snapshots by default? (cost vs restore window)
Edge case: ongoing long-running streams during cutover — should the controller wait for stream completion or force cutover?
Interplay with Dedicated reserved capacity: should we allow bypassing plan-lock for enterprise customers with strict IaC constraints?
